nice_title: Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management

first_line_treatment.indication: CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol (regardless of BP) OR CKD with hypertension
first_line_treatment.notes: Do not combine ACE-I + ARB. Monitor creatinine and potassium after 1-2 weeks

first_line_treatment.indication: CKD with ACR ≥22.6 mg/mmol, or eGFR 20-45
first_line_treatment.notes: NICE TA775. Slows CKD progression. Can use even without diabetes

first_line_treatment.indication: All CKD patients for cardiovascular risk reduction
first_line_treatment.notes: CKD is a cardiovascular risk equivalent

stage_1.management: Treat underlying cause, ACE-I/ARB if proteinuria, BP control, monitor annually

stage_2.management: As stage 1. Monitor eGFR 6-12 monthly. Address cardiovascular risk factors

stage_3a.management: Monitor eGFR every 6 months. Avoid nephrotoxins. Adjust drug doses. Refer if rapid decline (>5 ml/min/year)

stage_3b.management: As 3a. Prepare for possible RRT discussion. Check phosphate, calcium, PTH, bicarbonate. Anaemia screening

contraindicated_drugs.reason: Lactic acidosis risk (reduce dose if eGFR 30-45)
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and AKI
Risk of contrast nephropathy if eGFR <30

monitoring.stage_3b: eGFR and ACR every 3-6 months, plus bone profile, bicarbonate, Hb

referral_criteria: Sustained eGFR decline >5 ml/min/year: nephrology referral
Sustained eGFR decline ≥25% within 12 months (per NICE NG203)
non_pharmacological: Avoid nephrotoxic OTC medications (NSAIDs, herbal supplements)
